Task Name: T171 — T154's no-stale-frame property is true in the code and pinned by nothing
Description:
**Legacy ledger row:** `T171`

**Type / provenance:** Debt / test integrity

**Title:** T154's no-stale-frame property is true in the code and pinned by nothing

**Status at migration:** Filed (item 20, from T154's PASS)

---

**MINOR carried from T154's PASS, measured by the checker and worth more than its grade suggests.** Moving the re-seed out of the render body into a `useEffect` keyed on `[user, lastSeededUserId]` — a change that demonstrably reintroduces a stale frame — leaves **all 36 tests passing**. The property IS true in the shipped code (measured: commits are `["none:dark","user-bob:light"]` shipped vs `["none:dark","user-bob:dark","user-bob:light"]` under the mutation, the middle entry being Bob signed in with Alice's theme still on screen), but nothing would notice if it broke. **Two independent causes, both instructive.** (1) `RecordingProbe` consumes only `useThemeMode()`, and the provider's `useMemo(() => ({mode, refresh}), [mode, refresh])` memoizes the consumer away when `user` changes but `mode` does not — so a stale commit is structurally invisible to it. Only a **dual-context** recorder (`useThemeMode()` **and** `useAuth()`) can see it. (2) The test literally named `the stale theme never reaches the DOM even for one frame during the switch` does `renders.slice(beforeSwitch).filter((m) => m !== 'dark')` and asserts on the survivors — **it filters out the very value it should assert absent**, so `['dark','light']` passes. **This is the round-1 failure shape recurring inside the one test written to prevent it**, which is why it is filed rather than logged. Fix: dual-context recorder asserting `not.toContain('user-bob:dark')` on commits after the switch, and drop the `.filter`. Acceptance: moving the re-seed into a `useEffect` must fail the suite; it currently does not. The checker also corrected itself here — its own first strict `not.toContain('dark')` probe reported no stale frame under the mutation and was worthless for the same structural reason.

Task Name: T507 — The login card overflows the viewport on every phone narrower than ~400px
Description:
**Legacy ledger row:** `T507`

**Type / provenance:** Bug (responsive) — **found by the `layout-measurement` skill on its first run**

**Title:** The login card overflows the viewport on every phone narrower than ~400px

**Status at migration:** **Filed 2026-08-05 — MEASURED in real Chromium, not read from source**

---

`LoginPage.tsx:275` renders `<Card width={400} maxWidth="100%" padding={6}>`. **The author wrote the defensive `maxWidth` and it does nothing** — measured overflow by viewport: **320px → 40px · 360px → 20px · 375px → 13px · 390px → 5px · 414px and wider → 0**. So it affects most phones and worsens as the screen narrows; an iPhone SE is the worst case. **Presence-checked in the same run** (3 buttons, 2 inputs still rendered), so this is a real overflow and not the deleted-content artifact T325 caught. **Mechanism proven by walking the ancestor chain, not inferred:** the card is `rect=400 css-width=400px max-width=100%`, and its parent `.astryx-stack vertical` is **itself 400px with `max-width: none`** — so `100%` resolves against a box the card already sized, making the constraint a no-op. The first genuinely constrained ancestor is `.astryx-center` at 390px. **This is T325's exact mechanism on a second surface** (`maxWidth="100%"` resolving against an unconstrained parent, measured there as *no change*) — see T325's verification-log entry before packeting. **Candidate direction, not a prescription:** `maxWidth={400}` + `width="100%"` so the card fills the available width up to 400 rather than demanding 400 — but **measure it, do not assume it**; T325's obvious fix measured as a no-op. **No regression test is possible in jsdom** (no layout), so evidence is a before/after measurement, per the `layout-measurement` skill. **Not W2's surface** — `src/pages/login/**` belongs to no active workflow; needs an owner assignment before it is packeted.

Task Name: T512 — `WORKFLOWS.md`'s open-row counts are hand-recounted from the document itself; derive them from the ledger with a script instead
Description:
**Legacy ledger row:** `T512`

**Type / provenance:** Debt (process) — **filed 2026-08-05 on the owner's suggestion during PR #89 review**

**Title:** `WORKFLOWS.md`'s open-row counts are hand-recounted from the document itself; derive them from the ledger with a script instead

**Status at migration:** **Filed 2026-08-05**

---

**Filed because hand-recounting produced two wrong numbers in one PR.** `docs/swarm/WORKFLOWS.md`'s assignment table carries an open-row count per workflow. PR #89 recomputed those counts by reading `WORKFLOWS.md` — which is the artifact under repair — and shipped **two** defects the owner caught in review. (1) The helper treated `NARROWED` as a closed status, so T333 was silently dropped from every count and W9 read `3 — all human gates` while the same cell described T333's machine-workable ETL half. (2) The helper split the file into sections on `^## (W\d+) — `; W10 is the **last** workflow section, so its section ran to EOF and swallowed the Coordination-rules block-allocation table that follows, counting `T333`, `T600-699` and `T700-799` as W10 rows — W10 went 8 → 9 when the true figure was **6** (8 listed, T157 and T301 merged). Both defects are the same class: a count derived from prose, where a parsing miss produces a plausible number instead of an error. **The owner's framing, which is the fix:** *"the ledger is the only place a row's status actually lives, so counts belong derived from it — even a scripted count would beat hand-recounting a doc that four machines are appending to."* **Shape of the work:** a script reading `docs/swarm/task-ledger.md`'s pipe table (ID in column 1, Status in column 8), mapping each row ID to a workflow via the block allocation, and emitting open counts per workflow. Two requirements carried from the failures above — it must treat `NARROWED` as **open**, and it must **fail loudly** rather than return a number when a row ID maps to no workflow block or a status string matches none of the known keywords. A count that cannot be computed must say so; that is the same rule the `mutation-replay` skill enforces. Whether it runs in CI or by hand before a table edit is open. Suggested Allowed Files: `scripts/**`, `docs/swarm/WORKFLOWS.md`. **MEASURED 2026-08-05, and it raises the bar for this row: the table is NOT column-consistent, so "Status is column 8" is not a safe parse.** Splitting all 278 `|Tnnn|` rows on unescaped pipes gives **248 rows with the header's 10 columns, and 30 that disagree** — 2 with 9, 21 with 11, 6 with 12, 1 with 13. Found while updating T604 by column index: the patch asserted 10 columns and aborted rather than writing to the wrong cell. **A positional parser must therefore locate `Status` by header name and FAIL LOUDLY on any row whose column count does not match the header — never index blindly**, which is the same "a miss must error, not return a plausible number" requirement this row already carries. Normalising the 30 rows is the obvious companion fix and may be the cheaper half.

**Found while building T199's real `events` read, and T199 is what makes it observable** — before it the page had no rows at all, so nothing could be missing from them. `20260717000002_rls.sql:153-161`, verbatim: ```create policy own_or_linked_read on events for select to authenticated using (exists (select 1 from students s where s.id in (select my_student_ids()) and (events.team_ids is null or s.team_id = any(events.team_ids))));``` — and `event_sessions` (`:180-188`) inherits the identical test through `event_id`. **Both read the LEGACY single `students.team_id` column.** T187 (landed) moved `StudentHome` onto ACTIVE `student_teams` memberships (`StudentScope.teamIds`), so the page and the policy now scope by different sources. **They disagree for exactly one shape of user:** a dual-team student. An event scoped to `team_ids = {their SECOND team}` satisfies the page's `isEventInTeamScope` but is filtered out by RLS before it ever reaches the client — that student silently misses their second team's meetings, live check-in and sign-up opportunities. Constitution item 10 forbids editing the applied `20260717000002_rls.sql`, so this is a NEW file using `drop policy if exists` + `create policy`, the route `20260720000001_avatar_storage.sql` already establishes for policy replacement. Needs an RLS assertion suite (the `sql` CI job now runs 12 steps) proving a dual-team fixture student sees BOTH teams' events. **Owner applies the migration (item 16).** Also check `attendance`/`rsvps` policies for the same pattern before designing — this row only verified `events` and `event_sessions`.

Task Name: T807 — Two loaders still apply the `greatest(x, 1)` floor T509 removed, and three row types still declare `participation_pct` non-nullable
Description:

**Title:** Two loaders still apply the `greatest(x, 1)` floor T509 removed, and three row types still declare `participation_pct` non-nullable

**Status at migration:** **Filed 2026-08-07 (item 20). TypeScript-only — no migration.**

---

**Found while writing T199's own participation aggregate, by looking for an in-repo expression to reuse rather than inventing one (constitution item 3).** T509 (`20260806000000_met01_explicit_marks.sql`, APPLIED) replaced `v_student_participation`'s `round(100.0 * present_ct / greatest(expected_ct - excused_ct, 1), 1)` with an explicit `case when ... = 0 then null else round(...) end`, precisely so that a student whose every mark is `excused` stops reporting a fabricated `0.0%` and reports NULL (which the UI already renders as an em dash). **Two loaders re-apply the removed floor when they aggregate a dual-team student's per-team rows:** `loaders/meetings.ts:516` (`Math.max(expectedCt - excusedCt, 1)`, in `aggregateParticipationRows`) and `loaders/checkin.ts:375` (identical expression). Both comments cite the view's expression as their authority — that citation is now stale, and the citation being stale is what makes this hard to spot: the code looks correct and says why. **Behavioural consequence:** an all-excused student renders `—` on `ParticipationTab`/`StudentHome` (which read the view directly) and `0%` on `MeetingsList`/check-in (which go through these aggregates). Two screens, two different answers, for the case T509 exists to fix. **Three row types are also wrong at the type level:** `meetings.ts:283`, `checkin.ts:239` and `reports.ts:221` each declare `participation_pct: number` while the view can now return SQL NULL. `reports.ts`/`checkin.ts` happen to survive it (a null flows through the mapper and `ParticipationTab.tsx:830-831` renders `—`), so this is a lie in the types rather than a crash — but it is the lie that lets the two stale aggregates above look fine. T199's own `StudentHomeParticipationDbRow` types it `number | null` and returns `null` for the whole metric when the denominator is zero; that is the shape to converge on. **Consider widening `StudentParticipationMetric.participationPct` to `number | null`** — the shape is shared by `MeetingsList.tsx`, `StudentMeetingView.tsx`, `ParentHome.tsx` and `StudentHome.tsx` plus their tests, which is why T199 did not do it inline (item 25). **Verified before filing:** all five call sites read directly, and no later migration re-introduces the floor. **Not a migration** — T509's SQL is correct and applied; this is entirely TypeScript catching up to it.
